a simple depth normal consistency loss is sufficient to train both depth and surface normal estimation networks, that the depth network, when trained with this loss, significantly outperforms existing self-supervised depth estimation networks, that a network trained for surface normal prediction outperforms existing normal estimation networks, and finally that a network trained to estimate surface normals can be used for depth estimation as well.

we can train two Convolution Neural Networks (CNN), to predict depth and normals simultaneously, by imposing depth-normal consistency, and that the resulting normal network is state-of-the-art and the resulting depth network, relying only on smooth normal assumption, is much more accurate than traditional depth prediction networks.

(1) we propose a self-supervised framework to train a depth and a surface normal network simultaneously, (2) our normal network achieves state-of-the-art results on the KITTIDataset, and (3) our depth network, which relies on much more realistic smooth normal assumption and is trained with the proposed framework, outperforms existing self-supervised depth networks by a large margin.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our self-supervised depth network is more accurate than any other self-supervised method while our normal network is more accurate and robust than any supervised method on the same benchmark.
we show that the smoothness assumption on surface normals is a much better assumption to train a self-supervised depth network than piece-wise smooth depth assumption.

we present a novel self-supervised depth and normal estimation framework, which outperforms the state-of-the-art in both tasks, while also providing a much realistic smooth normal representation of outdoor scenes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the smooth normal assumption is a much stronger assumption compared to the smooth depth assumption.
the depth and normal estimation problems are tightly connected and can be solved simultaneously in a self-supervised fashion.
the surface normal assumption is more suitable to model natural scenes and can be effectively learnt in a self-supervised manner.
